from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.setup_layout("The Familiar World: Real Analysis", [

            "Sequences shrink as they approach a limit.",

        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        number_line = NumberLine(x_range=[-1, 3, 1], length=5, include_numbers=True)

        self.play(FadeIn(label))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "2-adic convergence requires differences divisible by high powers.",
            "Partial sums fill bits right to left.",
            "The sequence approaches a 2-adic limit."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Convergence under 2-adic Metric", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        powers = [2**i for i in range(1, 5)]
        bits = VGroup(*[Text(f"{p}", color=WHITE) for p in powers])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Represent sequence 2, 4, 8... on a line
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        for i, bit in enumerate(bits):
            self.place_at_grid(bit, f"A{i+1}", scale_factor=0.6)
            self.play(FadeIn(bit))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show distances shrinking towards zero
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF0000")
        
        arrows = VGroup()
        for i in range(len(bits)-1):
            arrow = Arrow(bits[i].get_bottom(), bits[i+1].get_bottom(), color="#FF0000")
            arrows.add(arrow)
            
        self.play(Create(arrows))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Display '2-adic limit is 0'
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        limit_text = Text("2-adic limit is 0", color="#FFFF00", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(limit_text, "E3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(limit_text))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Paradox: Infinite Sums", [
            "Geometric series 1+2+4+8 sums to negative one.",
            "Euclidean view explodes towards infinity.",
            "2-adic lens locks the sum at negative one."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        series = MathTex("1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + \\dots = S", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(series, "B2", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(series))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        euclidean_text = Text("Euclidean: S \\to \\infty", color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(euclidean_text, "C3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(euclidean_text))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        formula = MathTex("S = \\frac{1}{1-2} = -1", color="#FF00FF")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "D4", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        box = SurroundingRectangle(formula, color="#FF00FF", buff=0.1)
        self.play(FadeIn(formula), Create(box))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Conclusion", [
            "Convergence is defined by your metric choice.", 
            "2-adic metrics reveal hidden number structure.", 
            "Both Euclidean and 2-adic truths coexist."
        ])
        
        # Visual elements
        rabbit_carrot = VGroup(
            Dot(color=BLUE).scale(2), 
            Text("Rabbit", font_size=18).next_to(Dot(), UP)
        )
        binary_acc = VGroup(
            Square(color=RED, side_length=0.8),
            Text("-1", font_size=20)
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_at_grid(rabbit_carrot, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(binary_acc, "B5", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(rabbit_carrot), FadeIn(binary_acc))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.play(Indicate(rabbit_carrot), Indicate(binary_acc))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.play(FadeOut(rabbit_carrot), FadeOut(binary_acc))
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: Exploring the 2-adic Metric: Convergence in a Different World

sections.title: The Familiar World: Real Analysis
sections.content: Briefly review the standard Euclidean metric (distance) on real numbers. Visualize a sequence of numbers (e.g., 1/2, 1/4, 1/8...) shrinking toward 0 as the exponent increases.
sections.example: A rabbit jumping toward a carrot; each jump is half the previous distance. We see the rabbit clearly reaching the carrot at 0.

sections.title: Introducing the 2-adic Norm
sections.content: Define the 2-adic valuation |x|_2. Introduce the rule: a number is 'small' if it is divisible by a high power of 2. Contrast this with the Euclidean view.
sections.example: A digital 'filter' machine: Numbers are processed. 8 is considered 'small' (2^3), while 7 is considered 'large' (not divisible by 2). Visual: A bar chart where powers of 2 have shrinking heights.

sections.title: Convergence under 2-adic Metric
sections.content: Explain that in the 2-adic world, a sequence converges if the difference between successive terms is divisible by increasingly higher powers of 2. Show the sum 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + ...
sections.example: A 'Binary Accumulator' device. As we add terms, the bits fill up from right to left. The 'distance' to -1 becomes smaller in 2-adic space, even though the partial sums grow to infinity in Euclidean space.

sections.title: The Paradox: Infinite Sums
sections.content: Demonstrate the geometric series 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + ... = -1 in the 2-adic metric. Use the formula 1/(1-r) where r=2.
sections.example: A 'Mirror World' animation: In our standard view, the sum explodes to infinity. Through the 2-adic lens, the sum stabilizes at -1. Show a numerical 'lock' clicking into place at -1.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
sections.content: Recap that 'convergence' depends entirely on how we define 'distance'. 2-adic metrics are fundamental in number theory.
sections.example: A split-screen: Left side shows standard calculus (rabbit approaching carrot), right side shows 2-adic space (the binary accumulator clicking to -1). Both are valid mathematical truths.
